title: Nexus
description: Full-stack project management application with authentication, task tracking, Kanban board, and analytics. Built with Next.js App Router, Server Actions, and Prisma.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Nexus is a full-stack project management application built with Next.js 15 App Router. It covers authentication (Google OAuth + email/password), task and project management, a Kanban board, and an analytics dashboard with charts. The project started as a client-only frontend consuming an external REST API and has since been fully migrated to a server-first architecture using Server Components, Server Actions, and Prisma ORM.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: The goal was to build a production-grade application that goes beyond visual polish, addressing data architecture, server-side rendering, type-safe mutations, and authentication in a single cohesive Next.js project. It also served as a real migration exercise: replacing a separate backend, React Query, and Axios with Next.js built-in capabilities.
myFocus: Migrating from a client-side API-consuming frontend to a fullstack Next.js architecture with Server Components and Server Actions
Implementing Auth.js v5 with Google OAuth and email/password credentials, including password reset with email verification and rate limiting
Designing a type-safe Server Actions pattern with centralised ActionResult types and Zod validation
Building a co-located component and action architecture with per-feature subfolders and unit tests
whyThisStack: Next.js App Router enables Server Components and Server Actions, eliminating the need for a separate API layer and client-side state management library
Prisma ORM provides type-safe database access that integrates cleanly with TypeScript and keeps schema and queries in sync
Auth.js v5 handles the full authentication lifecycle (sessions, OAuth, and credentials) with Edge-compatible middleware for route protection
Zod ensures consistent validation across Server Actions and form inputs, with errors surfaced to the UI in a uniform pattern
keyFeatures: Google OAuth and email/password authentication with password reset flow and rate limiting
IDOR protection on all database queries, with every query scoped by userId
Task management with filtering, pagination, tagging, and status tracking
Analytics dashboard with priority distribution and tasks-by-status charts
Dark and light theme with mobile-responsive layout and drawers
Reusable Server Actions with centralised ActionResult type and Zod validation
challengesTradeoffs: Migrating incrementally from React Query and Axios to Server Actions without breaking existing features
Designing a scalable actions architecture, splitting monolithic files into co-located per-action modules with tests
Balancing server-side simplicity with client interactivity using the 'use client' boundary carefully
whatILearned: Server Components significantly reduce client bundle size and remove the need for explicit loading state management in most cases
Co-locating actions and tests in per-feature subfolders makes the codebase easier to navigate and reduces friction when adding tests
A centralised ActionResult type with consistent Zod validation across all Server Actions prevents a whole class of runtime errors
nextSteps: Add E2E tests with Playwright covering the auth flow and critical user paths
Implement saved views, recurring tasks, and subtask support
Add email digest and keyboard shortcut support
Explore SaaS foundations: multi-user workspaces and billing

title: Redirect Lab
description: Full-stack link management platform with custom short URLs, access tracking, cross-tab synchronisation, accessible interactions, infinite scrolling, and CSV export through Cloudflare R2.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Redirect Lab is a full-stack link management platform built with an independent React client and Fastify API. It evolved from Brev.ly, a postgraduate coursework project created to explore full-stack development and AWS. The original monorepo remains archived, while Redirect Lab introduces a new identity, independently deployable repositories, stronger accessibility and testing practices, and a cost-conscious cloud architecture.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: The goal was to transform an academic URL shortener into a maintainable portfolio product with a focused user experience, reliable state handling, automated quality checks, independent delivery pipelines, and infrastructure that can operate at little or no cost.
myFocus: Separating the original monorepo into independent client and server repositories while preserving its development history
Rebranding the product and refining the complete link creation, management, redirection, and export experience
Improving accessibility with semantic controls, focus management, descriptive labels, and axe-based component tests
Synchronising access counts across browser tabs with BroadcastChannel without introducing additional real-time infrastructure
Migrating deployment from AWS to a cost-conscious architecture using Vercel, Railway, Neon, and Cloudflare R2
whyThisStack: React and TanStack Query provide a focused client architecture with explicit server-state caching, mutation feedback, and paginated data loading
Fastify and Drizzle ORM create a lightweight, type-safe API and persistence layer that stays aligned with the TypeScript domain model
Vitest, Testing Library, and axe-core support fast behavioral and accessibility testing without introducing external testing services
Vercel, Railway, Neon, and Cloudflare R2 provide independently deployable infrastructure with practical free or low-cost tiers
keyFeatures: Custom short URL creation with validation and duplicate prevention
Redirection to original URLs with access count tracking
Cross-tab access count synchronisation through BroadcastChannel
Paginated link loading with infinite scrolling and IntersectionObserver
CSV export stored on Cloudflare R2 and delivered through a public URL
Contextual loading states and success/error feedback for link mutations
Accessible forms, dialogs, controls, focus states, and automated axe checks
Automated pull request validation with tests, type-checking, and linting
challengesTradeoffs: Separating the original monorepo while preserving history and allowing the client and API to evolve independently
Replacing the original AWS delivery setup with lower-cost services without losing deployment reliability
Keeping access counts synchronised across tabs without adding WebSockets or an external real-time service
Protecting delivery scope by postponing authentication and advanced analytics until the core product is stable
whatILearned: Independent repositories make ownership, documentation, deployment, and release cycles clearer for full-stack projects
BroadcastChannel can solve cross-tab synchronisation elegantly when full real-time infrastructure would be unnecessary
Testing interaction states and accessibility behavior provides more confidence than testing implementation details
Infrastructure decisions should balance technical capability, operational complexity, and the realistic cost of maintaining a portfolio product
nextSteps: Build an access analytics dashboard with clicks grouped by period
Add QR Code generation and PNG download
Support optional link expiration with a dedicated expired state
Add a UTM parameter builder with URL preview
Allow editing the destination URL of an existing short link
Add inline copy feedback and bulk deletion
